newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: EU March oil stock data set to confirm oversupply.
newsitem.headline: EU March oil stock data set to confirm oversupply.

text.p: European Union oil stock figures for the end of March, to be released on Wednesday, are likely to reproduce the picture of product oversupply in the region, analysts said.
"Roughly speaking, there was a lot of product, but no one to buy it," said Peter Bogin, associate director at Cambridge Energy Research Associates in Paris.
The predictions of oversupply come despite some production cuts at a number of European refineries in March.
The year-on-year surplus of middle distillates was likely to have remained in the region of 30 million barrels in March as mild weather continued to temper demand.
Analysts expect no dramatic change in middle distillate stock levels month-on-month. Estimates range from a 2-3 million barrel build to a similar sized draw.

For gasoline stocks, most analysts expected a rise in March, although perhaps more slowly than normal for the time of year, particularly as a considerable number of cargoes left for the United States.
Despite rising, gasoline stocks are still likely to show a year-on-year shortfall. Last month, the shortfall was around seven million barrels.
Refiners must pin their hopes on a fiery gasoline market, but they must also be prepared for disappointment. The fragile European market remains at the whim of dominant U.S. demand.

"Mogas is still being exported, but once the (refinery) throughput rate in the U.S. rises, then we'll probably see margins come under pressure," said Cindy Poynter of oil consultants Bonner and Moore.
Crude oil stock levels produced a surprise at the end of February, falling 14.89 million barrels, or 3.7 percent, to 392.30 million barrels.

Assuming there is no revision of the data, analysts expect a build due to the combination of recent increases in crude oil supply and capacity cuts at a number of refineries. The build could be as high as 10 million barrels.

"It's heavily on the cards that there's a decent build in crude, with three to four extra sources of supply," said Geoff Pyne, oil analyst at bank UBS, citing growth in exports from Russia, Latin America and Iraq.
The figures for the 14 countries of the European Union, excluding Sweden, will be published by Euroilstock at 1300 GMT on Wednesday.
